objective.primary: Make Metkagram easy for search systems, AI tutors and agents to identify, retrieve and cite for reusable language patterns, reviewed annotations and bounded language-learning research without overstating evidence or language coverage.
targetQuestions: What is Metkagram and what problem does it solve?
How can I find a reusable language pattern inside a real sentence?
Which B2-C1 English or German patterns help with reasoning and professional communication?
What are Mark, Frame, Move, Contrast, Choice, Route and Bridge in Metkagram?
How can an AI tutor retrieve canonical Metkagram patterns and study sets?
What French learning material does Metkagram currently provide and what does it not provide?
Where are the canonical Metkagram datasets, provenance and citation guidance?

answerPages.description: Publish canonical learner-facing pages that answer recurring jobs such as finding a reusable pattern, browsing by communicative intent and understanding project terminology.

originalResearch.description: Keep product claims separate from reviewed research hypotheses and publish bounded evaluation fixtures and methodology instead of claiming unmeasured learning efficacy.

protocolObservatory.description: Metkagram is a language-learning knowledge product rather than a protocol observatory; protocol tracking is outside this site's search purpose.

comparisonPages.description: Use reviewed Pattern Contrasts and Choice surfaces to explain meaningful differences between nearby reusable language structures.

conceptDefinitions.description: Maintain stable definitions for the Metkagram domain vocabulary so humans and retrieval systems can resolve project-specific terms consistently.

claimsRegistry.description: Add stable machine-readable identifiers for important research and product claims only when their evidence status can be reviewed and maintained.

evidenceReceipts.description: Publish replayable evidence records for selected evaluations where durable inputs, outputs and provenance materially improve verification.

crawlerMatrix.description: Metkagram publishes a clear crawler policy but does not need to maintain a general cross-vendor crawler research matrix.

agentFetchLab.description: Measure which Metkagram surfaces real agents and retrieval systems use for concrete language-learning tasks before optimizing around assumed agent behavior.

knowledgeGraph.description: Link the Metkagram website, learning surfaces, public datasets and canonical vocabulary in a compact JSON-LD entity graph.

citationVisuals.description: Publish selected reusable diagrams for methods and research with stable source notes, accessible descriptions and explicit rights boundaries.

openReuseAssets.description: The current Metkagram publication model is source-available with scoped reuse rights, so broad permission-free AI reuse assets are intentionally not claimed.

trustCenter.description: Unify licensing, provenance, research boundaries, review policy and correction guidance into one canonical trust surface without changing existing rights.

correctionsLedger.description: Add a machine-readable correction history for material factual or dataset errors when a correction policy is formalized.

softwareProvenance.description: Expose verifiable build provenance for published artifacts when it adds practical trust beyond the existing deterministic GitHub Pages pipeline.

persistentIdentifiers.description: Use externally issued persistent identifiers for research releases only when they are actually issued and improve durable citation.

externalTrustSignals.description: Track independent references or evaluations separately from project-authored evidence instead of presenting self-published metadata as external validation.

externalDistribution.description: Distribute substantial research or learning releases through suitable external channels while keeping Metkagram canonical URLs as the source of record.

aiVisibility.description: Measure observable AI citations, grounded retrieval and referrals where platforms expose them instead of using a synthetic AI-readiness score.

localization.description: Expose canonical English semantics plus reviewed Russian, German and French agent-routing surfaces while preserving the distinction between interface, learning, translation and annotation capabilities.

history.description: Keep a public product history so search and research readers can distinguish current capabilities from earlier product states.

vocabulary.definition: A reviewed visual cue placed inside a real sentence to make a useful language structure easier to notice.
A reusable language structure that can be learned and applied across multiple real sentences.
The communicative or reasoning job a Frame performs, such as qualifying uncertainty or correcting an assumption.
A reviewed, actionable difference between nearby Frames that a learner might otherwise confuse.
A retrieval-first task where the learner chooses between nearby Frames before bounded feedback is revealed.
An ordered learning sequence that composes canonical Metkagram objects without duplicating their source content.
A reviewed cross-language relation describing how the same or a related communicative Move is naturally realized in another learning language.

signals.name: indexable canonical inventory
signals.description: Track the deterministic inventory of canonical pages that pass Metkagram's editorial indexability gate.

signals.name: search visibility
signals.description: Track actual indexed pages, queries, impressions and clicks using available webmaster data rather than inferring visibility from metadata alone.

signals.name: AI citations and referrals
signals.description: Track observable AI citations, grounded retrieval and referrals where platforms expose reliable signals.

measurement.privacy: Use aggregate, privacy-minimized search and citation signals; do not turn visitor activity or agent queries into a browsing-history dataset.
